summary: Earth Spins is a retro web jukebox that lets you hear them. Pick a NASA Earth visualization (with ID) and press START. Gemini 3.8 Flash watches the first 30 seconds of the video, summarizes into a music prompt, and compose into 30-second instrumental tracks: Part 1 by Google Lyria 2, Part 2 by Meta MusicGen. Blind and low-vision users, and anyone who finds charts hard to read, can now explore Earth data by ear, and every play has a short share link.
details:
What it does:

Pick a NASA Earth visualization (topic dial search or SVS ID) and the jukebox composes music for it.

You Have to Try It! https://nasa2026.scsonic.com

How it works:

1. Backend server Reads the title, description, image and video from the NASA SVS API.

2. Gemini 3.8 Flash is an omni-modal that can understand video. It analyzes the first 30 seconds, summarizes what happens, identifies key changes and trends, and combines these insights with information from the webpage to generate a six-section music prompt covering mood, tempo, key, instruments, and more.

3. Lyria 2 composes Part 1 in under a minute. MusicGen generates Part 2 using a Colab GPU, which takes about 3 minutes. Each generation produces a completely new and unique composition.

Benefits:

Earth data for blind and low-vision users; a fun, shareable way into climate science; open prompts show what the SI read from the data.


What is the intended impact of the project?

AI-powered visual understanding goes beyond pixel-to-sound mapping, analyzing image features, motion, and environmental changes to compose expressive, integrated music.

Considerations:

1. Flexible Input: Accepts a wide variety of visualization videos.

2. Authentic UI: A jukebox-inspired interface with intuitive controls.

3. Easy Sharing: Share generated music with friends via short URLs.

Tools:

Claude, Antigravity, Python, FastAPI, SQLite, ffmpeg, HTML/CSS/JS, Google Vertex AI (Gemini 3.8 Flash, Lyria 2), Meta MusicGen on Google Colab.

Code:

https://github(dot)com(slash)scsonic(slash)nasa2026

Show Case (right click open in new windows or copy url):

Daily Polar Sea Ice, Two Year History (SVS 5099)

https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/wtqpq

Arctic and Antarctic ice take turns: high celesta and low cello breathe in opposite phase, one cycle per year.

Global Temperature Anomalies 1880–2023 (SVS 5207)

https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/npjpr

143 years of warming: cool hesitant strings climb slowly, then surge into blazing brass for 2023's record heat.

Sea Level Through a Porthole (SVS 5235)

https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/bqapb

A rolling harp ostinato for endless waves, stepping quietly higher each section as the sea keeps rising.

Safeguarding the U.S. East Coast from Hurricanes (SVS 14369)

https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/dhvys

Spinning violin spirals over a hot-ocean drone; the bass marches north with Earl as Fiona's spiral begins anew.

Particulate Matter PM2.5 (SVS 5151)

https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/xmqub

A hazy 3/4 waltz: every bar is one day of pollution pulse, while a flute drifts like dust on wind.

TEMPO Nitrogen Dioxide over North America (SVS 5175)

https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/hxrtv

Sunrise arpeggios, buzzing rush-hour bursts and silent nights trace three days of city pollution seen by TEMPO.


https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/gokfo

A bouncy, zigzagging melody with rapid pitch changes.

We also included SVS ID from the resources to create new music. Try different vibes!


  1. Data Sonification: Caldwell 73 (SVS 13786)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/tvfhs

  A radar sweeps once around a star cluster: blue stars ring glockenspiel, red stars marimba, pitch rising outward.

  2. GEDI Forest Height (SVS 4950)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/nfbjx

  As Earth turns, marimba layers grow with forest height, peaking when the towering Amazon rainforest rises into view.

  3. A 3D View of an Atmospheric River (SVS 4960)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/rbasq

  Strings open as the camera pulls back, then one long melody flows like a river of moisture toward America.

  4. Lightning Events Detected from the ISS 2017–2023 (SVS 5011)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/czakl

  A synth sweep every nine seconds marks each ISS orbit; crackling electric plucks are lightning over the tropics.

  5. DYAMOND Global Carbon Dioxide (SVS 5196)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/xakox

  Smoldering brass and gritty synths swell at each carbon dioxide hotspot: East Asia, Africa's fires, then Brazil.

  6. Change in Night Lights between 2012 and 2023 (SVS 5313)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/evwhh

  One chord per year of city lights; rising vibraphone marks brighter places, falling horn the regions that dimmed.

  7. Perpetual Ocean 2: Western Boundary Currents (SVS 5425)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/ukyqx

  Endless harp shimmer for swirling eddies; the melody grows strongest as the Gulf Stream comes into view.

  8. GEOS Aerosols (2025) (SVS 5669)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/mjkdb

  9. Air Quality Model Runs (SVS 5533)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/orgad

  Four instruments, four pollutants, one interlocking groove that grows louder and grittier through the 2024 fire season.

  

  10. Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature (SVS 3912)

  https://nasa2026.scsonic.com/share/hfdtq

  A never-ending harp and cello flow; a brightening flute traces cool water stretching west across the Pacific.

Project Limitations: AI may interpret videos differently each time, focusing on different visual elements. As a result, the generated music style and composition may vary. Try generating multiple times to explore different interpretations.

That's why we invited two different composers(Lyria and MusicGen) to create the music.
